steps.note: Compatibility layer, no data touched: in one short transaction rename the table orders -> orders_base and put an auto-updatable view named orders in its place that exposes the column both as amount and as total (same base column). Old app replicas (amount) and new ones (total) both keep working through the view. The ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is taken with a 150ms lock_timeout and retried, so live queries are never queued behind us for long.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND attname = 'amount' AND NOT attisdropped) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'public.orders.amount not found'; END IF; IF to_regclass('public.orders_base') IS NOT NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'public.orders_base already exists'; END IF; PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '150ms', true); LOOP BEGIN LOCK TABLE public.orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE public.orders RENAME TO orders_base; CREATE VIEW public.orders AS SELECT id, customer_id, amount, status, email, created_at, amount AS total FROM public.orders_base; ALTER VIEW public.orders ALTER COLUMN id SET DEFAULT nextval('public.orders_id_seq'::regclass); ALTER VIEW public.orders ALTER COLUMN created_at SET DEFAULT now(); EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 300 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Check the view works for reads by both names before switching the app.
steps.sql: SELECT id, amount, total FROM public.orders ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1; DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.orders WHERE id = (SELECT max(id) FROM public.orders) AND amount IS DISTINCT FROM total) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'view mismatch'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Rolling update: the app now reads and writes total (via the view). Old and new replicas can run side by side.
Let terminating old pods (which still use amount) finish draining (3s drain + in-flight, 30s grace period) before amount disappears.

Final switch, no data touched: in one short transaction drop the view, rename orders_base back to orders and rename its column amount -> total (metadata only: same type, NOT NULL, same data, same pkey/sequence). Same short lock_timeout + retry. Lock on the view first (it propagates to the base table), the same order live queries use.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN IF to_regclass('public.orders_base') IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'public.orders_base not found'; END IF; PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '150ms', true); LOOP BEGIN LOCK TABLE public.orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; DROP VIEW public.orders; ALTER TABLE public.orders_base RENAME TO orders; ALTER TABLE public.orders RENAME COLUMN amount TO total; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 300 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Verify the end state: orders is a table again, total is numeric(10,2) NOT NULL, amount is gone, no leftover view/table.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF (SELECT relkind FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'public.orders'::regclass) <> 'r' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders is not a table'; END IF; IF to_regclass('public.orders_base') IS NOT NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders_base still exists'; END IF; IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND attname = 'total' AND NOT attisdropped AND attnotnull AND format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) = 'numeric(10,2)') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.total is not numeric(10,2) NOT NULL'; END IF; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND attname = 'amount' AND NOT attisdropped) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.amount still exists'; END IF; END $$; SELECT id, total FROM public.orders ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;
